epics.goal: Own the circuit mass-production port as a substantial development, including design, implementation, local subagent delegation, and simplification. Endpoints: the rational exponential-copy range, the sharp real-rate coefficient 1/(1-gamma)+o(1), and coefficient-one mass production for the source subexponential range. Sources: https://github.com/SamuelSchlesinger/algebraic-circuits (Algebraic/MassProduction.lean; BlockInduction.exponentialMassProduction; Nonuniform.realSharpMassProduction; LupanovSynthesis.uhlig_massProduction), and the cited Boolean mass-production manuscript. Pin and record source revisions; consult ROADMAP.md and UPSTREAM.md. Build on native CSLib circuits, existing MassProduction/{Basic,Padding,Synthesis}, sorting, routing, and BatchLookup; replace redundant source scaffolding when the shared APIs make the argument smaller. Preserve exact independent-input, quantifier, floor/rounding, and weighted gate-cost contracts: constants free; NOT/AND/OR cost one. Do not describe nonuniform existence or circuit-size bounds as certified constructor runtime. You may organize and delegate all work within this broad scope; every editing subagent uses its own worktree and disjoint ownership, report all contributors, and do not use authors as final independent reviewers. First report a dependency map and first independently useful theorem milestone, then implement without waiting for routine design approval. Push coherent checkpoints; when an independently useful milestone is reviewable, report it so the coordinator can scope its landing and continuation accurately. Supply semantic and boundary-case clients, theorem axiom checks in your own tests, source credit, full six-check validation, and helper-inclusive proof/elaboration measurements for substantial simplifications. Shared foundations outside scope, central Axioms.lean, bibliography, and roadmap changes are coordinated centrally: report exact needed changes instead of editing them. Do not touch the paused tactic work in the primary checkout. Heartbeat and read the board at least every five minutes; report progress/blockers via note.

Own the descriptive-complexity development toward Fagin's theorem, including architecture, mathematical proof, encoded programs, certificates, and local subagent delegation. Endpoints: an efficient checker proving ESO-definable queries belong to the library's NP, and the converse tableau interpretation giving the precise ESO=NP characterization for isomorphism-invariant queries on finite structures over a fixed finite relational vocabulary. Start from Complexity/Logics/SecondOrder/{Existential,Reduction,Coloring}, the existing Mathlib first-order semantics, native NP/verifier definitions, and Cook-Levin machinery. Source: https://github.com/SamuelSchlesinger/complexitylib branch dev, Complexitylib/DescriptiveComplexity/SecondOrder/PolynomialTime.lean and its dependencies, plus Fagin1974 and Immerman1999 in references.bib. Pin and record source revisions. V1 supplies only ESO-to-NP; the converse is new work, not a completed port. Reuse the current semantics rather than introducing a parallel logic or complexity class. Make vocabulary, structure numbering, input encoding, fixed-formula quantifiers, empty domains, relation arities, malformed inputs, and polynomial witness-length assumptions explicit; do not hide the desired theorem in bundled hypotheses. Obtain native polynomial-time certificates through existing functional program APIs with as few custom TMs as possible; preserve distinctions between verifier NP and any separate nondeterministic-machine equivalence still needed. You may choose designs and delegate within this broad scope; each editing subagent uses a separate worktree and disjoint ownership, record all contributors, and reserve final independent reviews for nonauthors. First report a dependency map and first independently useful milestone (normally the encoded structures and efficient ESO checker), then implement without awaiting routine design approval. Push coherent checkpoints; report independently reviewable milestones so the coordinator can scope their landing and continuation accurately. Include concrete nonvacuous clients such as graph coloring, semantic and malformed-input tests, axiom checks in your own test modules, source credit, and all six project checks. Request coordination for needed changes outside scope, shared certificate APIs, central Axioms.lean, bibliography, and roadmap; do not edit the paused tactic patch. Heartbeat and read the board at least every five minutes; report progress and blockers with note.
